title: Qi-Gong with Cody
location: Wellness Collective, 76 S 100 W, Moab, UT 84532
description: Zhineng Qigong is a powerful mind-body practice rooted in ancient Chinese healing traditions and adapted for modern times. This gentle yet profound system blends slow movement, sound, visualization, and meditation to help individuals cultivate inner peace, restore balance, and enhance vitality. By consciously connecting with the energy of life—what some may call qi or universal life force—participants are invited into a process of holistic healing: physically, emotionally, and spiritually. One of the most accessible forms of Qigong, Zhineng emphasizes connection over complexity. Its principles can be embraced by people of all ages, backgrounds, and physical abilities. Cody teaches from a place of lived experience, having found this practice deeply healing and transformative in his own journey. His classes focus on cultivating shared energy through group practice, empowering individuals to tap into their innate wisdom and live with greater purpose and presence.

title: Tai Chi with Drew
location: Wellness Collective, 76 S 100 W, Moab, UT 84532
description: Among all forms of physical activity, Tai Chi Ch’uan is perhaps the most accessible, convenient, and economical way to improve both physical health and mental well-being. As Yang Style Tai Chi master Cheng Man-Ching once said, ‘Those who understand the importance of exercise for health will find Tai Chi Ch’uan indispensable.’ While Tai Chi may not be easy to master, consistent practice will yield results. In this class, we will focus on cultivating chi, building endurance and strength, and developing core alignment, all while learning to release tension. Tai Chi training offers many levels of progression. In Yang Style, when practiced correctly, it becomes an aerobic workout, despite minimal movement. Additionally, it serves as a form of meditation. Please wear comfortable clothing. Flat shoes, socks, or bare feet are ideal. Students are encouraged to train at their own pace, and progression will vary from person to person.

title: Qi-Gong with Cody
location: Wellness Collective, 76 S 100 W, Moab, UT 84532
description: Zhineng Qigong is a powerful mind-body practice rooted in ancient Chinese healing traditions and adapted for modern times. This gentle yet profound system blends slow movement, sound, visualization, and meditation to help individuals cultivate inner peace, restore balance, and enhance vitality. By consciously connecting with the energy of life—what some may call qi or universal life force—participants are invited into a process of holistic healing: physically, emotionally, and spiritually. One of the most accessible forms of Qigong, Zhineng emphasizes connection over complexity. Its principles can be embraced by people of all ages, backgrounds, and physical abilities. Cody teaches from a place of lived experience, having found this practice deeply healing and transformative in his own journey. His classes focus on cultivating shared energy through group practice, empowering individuals to tap into their innate wisdom and live with greater purpose and presence.

title: Tai Chi with Drew
location: Wellness Collective, 76 S 100 W, Moab, UT 84532
description: Among all forms of physical activity, Tai Chi Ch’uan is perhaps the most accessible, convenient, and economical way to improve both physical health and mental well-being. As Yang Style Tai Chi master Cheng Man-Ching once said, ‘Those who understand the importance of exercise for health will find Tai Chi Ch’uan indispensable.’ While Tai Chi may not be easy to master, consistent practice will yield results. In this class, we will focus on cultivating chi, building endurance and strength, and developing core alignment, all while learning to release tension. Tai Chi training offers many levels of progression. In Yang Style, when practiced correctly, it becomes an aerobic workout, despite minimal movement. Additionally, it serves as a form of meditation. Please wear comfortable clothing. Flat shoes, socks, or bare feet are ideal. Students are encouraged to train at their own pace, and progression will vary from person to person.
